key_insight: Rather than committing to one generated action, an LLM agent can generate several options at each turn and use a second model to choose one. The paper evaluates this turn-level best-of-N approach; the provided abstract does not include performance results.
problem_solved: How to use additional inference-time computation to improve action selection in complex, long-horizon agent tasks.
method: At each turn, a generator LLM proposes N candidate actions.
A selector LLM chooses one candidate, which is executed in the environment.
Repeat this generate–select–execute loop throughout the task.
impact: This offers practitioners a straightforward way to spend extra inference compute on agent decisions without changing model weights. Its practical value depends on measured performance gains relative to added generation and selection costs.
visual_elements: Flow diagram: task state → N candidate actions → selector → executed action → updated state.
Branching action tree with the selected action highlighted and alternatives faded.
Long-horizon timeline showing selection repeated at every turn.
Compute-budget illustration contrasting one candidate with N candidates plus a selection step.
paper_title: On Turn-Level Best-of-N Sampling for Scaling LLM Agents
paper_authors: Jalaj Bhandari, Dhawal Gupta, Hongli Zhan, Zhenting Wang, Varad Pimpalkhute
